scripts.//gate: Runs test:coverage, not test -- the thresholds in jest.config.cjs are enforced by nothing otherwise, and main once sat 30 points under one of them without anybody knowing. Hosted CI runs this same script, so the two cannot disagree.
scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run test:coverage
scripts.//test:e2e: The E2E tier. Needs the compose Postgres (npm run db:up) and a migrated schema. Builds and starts its own server on :3100 rather than reusing one -- a suite that passes against a stale server proves nothing about this commit.
scripts.//test:integration: Real PostgreSQL. Needs `npm run db:up && npm run db:migrate` first. Not in `gate`: it needs a daemon, and a gate that fails for environmental reasons is one people route around.
scripts.//verify:schema: Applies the migration to a throwaway postgres and races the first-admin index. Needs docker; needs no provisioned database. Not in `gate` because it is slow and needs a daemon -- run it whenever prisma/ changes.
scripts.//pretype-check: Generate the Prisma client BEFORE anything type-checks it. Without this a clean clone fails with a dozen `implicitly has an any type` errors while every machine that has ever installed passes -- the client is generated into the hoisted root node_modules, and the types it emits are what `tsc` reads. This repo's README already tells that story once; this is the line that stops it happening a third time.
